ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 1.5:1 ratio of high-intensity white (pixel values ~210-245) to low-intensity black (pixel values ~10-40) across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white regions occupy the central areas of both lobes. Heavy black pigmentation borders the entire trailing edge and central notch, with asymmetrical 'finger-like' dark extensions protruding into the white field on the inner-right lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an internal angle of approximately 42 degrees and a bounding-box depth occupying roughly 18% of the visible vertical fluke profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular trailing edge with frequent high-frequency serrations (2-10 pixel amplitude) along distal edges; larger, jagged peaks and valleys are concentrated near the medial notch transition.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex sweep from the medial to distal regions, terminating in relatively sharp, tapered tips with an increased rate of curvature at the outer 15% of the span.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Visible high-contrast white circular pixel clusters on the dark leading edge of the left lobe and scattered dark circular spots on the white surface of the upper left lobe tip.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Three distinct, roughly parallel dark linear disruptions (rake marks) situated on the inner-trailing edge of the right lobe, cutting approximately 150 pixels into the white pigment field.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Notable rake marks on the right lobe and white barnacle-site scarring on the left leading edge; minor distal tip erosion visible on the left lobe tip.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced asymmetrical black pigmentation encroachment on the inner right lobe compared to the relatively clean white-to-black boundary on the inner left lobe.
